issuer: the Inland Revenue Department, with the tests held by the Licensing Authority
note: Read 2026-10-30 on sknird.com, the Inland Revenue Department's own site. A learner's authority is issued from 17 (EC$62.50 a year, not held) and, after the written and road tests, the licence is issued at the Department on payment of the required fees, so it is held from 17; a permanent licence is valid for at most three years (as little as two, depending on when it was renewed) and expires on the holder's birthday, kept as 3 years. The first licence's fee isn't stated (a renewal costs EC$187.50, not held), so it is null. The identity card is not this office's.

sources.title: Inland Revenue Department, St Kitts and Nevis, Driver's Licence
sources.said: The applicant must be at least seventeen (17) years of age at the time of the application. ... a Certificate of Competency is issued and must be collected from the Inland Revenue Department, where after payment of the required fees, the drivers licence is issued. ... A permanent drivers licence is valid for a maximum period of three years and as little as two years, depending on the date it was renewed.
